description: F-CORE-035: what a tenant is configured as is readable. Since SPEC-015 the library stores four things about a tenant's setup — tax profile, dimension master data, allocation scheme, imported mappings — and reported exactly one of them back (the tax profile, through `systemDescription`). The other three could be written and never read. The seed rule from the same release is what makes that worse than an ordinary gap: before it, an embedding passed its cost centres in on every open and its own copy was the truth by construction; now the stored record wins from the second open on, so summae's copy is the truth and the embedding's is a guess it cannot check. A screen with a cost-centre field could learn the accepted values only by posting and reading `E_DIMENSION_INVALID`. The projection reports what is IN FORCE, not what is stored, and the two places they differ are the point: `dimensionRules` come from the pack and stand in no record at all, and `mappings` lists the pack's alongside the imported ones — mirroring the record would answer "none" for a tenant whose balanceSheet, incomeStatement and cashBasisReport all work. Mapping identity only, never the positions: those are the pack's, which the embedding holds and summae deliberately keeps no copy of.

steps.comment: The tenant's own master data. Declared through the OPERATION rather than in the setup, because that is the case which used to be stored and unreadable.
Declared second, reported first: the master data comes back sorted by code, not in the order it was declared.
An import on top of the pack's mapping. Both have to show up below — the record holds only this one, so a projection mirroring the record would hide the pack's.

expect.comment: Die vier gespeicherten Dinge plus das, was aus dem Pack gilt — die Frage „als was ist dieser Mandant eingerichtet", die vorher nur zum Steuerprofil beantwortet war. `smallBusiness: []` ist die Serialisierung von „nie erklärt": das Profil führt Segmente mit Gültigkeitsbeginn, und ein `false` im Setup erklärt keines.
